# Interactive daemon manager

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships `codegraph daemon` with alias `daemons` as an interactive manager for background daemons, showing the current project first and allowing stop-one or stop-all. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says this replaces hunting for a pid and killing it by hand.

# Sibling exemplar selection

Lifecycle status: proposed

When no interceptor or sibling implementation is on the spine, adaptive explore may need to show one forced exemplar instead of skeletonizing all siblings. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says all siblings skeletonize today in this case and a forced exemplar might read better, but it is untested.

# Project-local config auto-wiring

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph init` auto-wires project-local agent configuration for agents previously installed globally, so a global install applies in each opened project without per-project reinstall. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 says one global `codegraph install` works in every project you open because `codegraph init` wires project-local agent config for globally installed agents.

Lifecycle status: accepted

The installer passes the correct project path into Cursor's MCP config so globally installed CodeGraph resolves the workspace even when Cursor launches MCP servers with the wrong working directory. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 Fixes says this works around Cursor launching MCP servers with the wrong working directory and fixes global installs reporting `not initialized` in every workspace.

# Project-name-neutral intent ranking

Lifecycle status: accepted

Search ranking should not let a repo-wide project name overpower the query terms that identify the actual code area. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 says users naturally include the project name in queries, but it over-weighted matching paths and buried the backend in mixed-stack repos until project-name terms were neutralized for path scoring and type-disambiguation bias.

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Measure before assuming holes

Lifecycle status: accepted

Measure framework usage before assuming a dynamic-dispatch hole; Svelte's presumed event-handler gap was not the real gap because modern Svelte often uses form actions and callback props instead of `on:click={fn}`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 explicitly states this lesson in the Svelte/SvelteKit row.

# Declared return types define chain fit

Lifecycle status: accepted

The lesson from #750 is that chained-call support fits languages with reliably declared return types, not the broader or narrower label of statically typed languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says the original statically-typed README enumeration was incomplete and the through-line is reliable declared return types.

# Constant read node check

Lifecycle status: accepted

A new value-reference language must confirm the grammar node type used for constant reads before sweeping, because a reader-scan mismatch produces zero edges even when targets register correctly. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A names this as the PHP lesson: PHP constant references are `name` nodes, not `identifier` or `constant`, so edges did not form until `name` was added to `flushValueRefs`.

# Parent-kind sample check

Lifecycle status: accepted

Before enabling value references for the next class-scope language, inspect the parent kind of a sample constant and widen the target gate when that shared parent kind is missing. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A explicitly calls this the lesson for the next class-scope language and says missing `struct:`, `enum:`, or `interface:`-style parent kinds make the feature silently emit nothing despite nodes existing.

# Trace wrongness masquerades as adoption floor

Lifecycle status: accepted

A small repo read-heavy result can be a fixable trace endpoint bug rather than an adoption floor; compare what the agent read with the tool output immediately before it. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3d says Alamofire was misread as the small-repo floor until transcripts showed the tool returned wrong stub endpoints, and the methodology lesson says transcript reasoning, not the median, tells which case it is.

# Value-ref false-positive handling

Lifecycle status: accepted

During value-reference validation, false-positive clusters must be fixed while isolated singletons are recorded as known residuals. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 instructs agents to hunt FPs during the validation sweep, fix FP clusters, and record singletons.

# Pascal case-sensitive misses

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference scanning may miss references that differ only by case because Pascal is case-insensitive while the reader scan matches exact text; this is a false negative, not a false positive. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says differently-cased Pascal references are missed and not worth normalizing.

# Sibling class constant ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file-wide class-scope target map accepts a residual false-positive risk when sibling classes in the same file define the same constant name. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says this is the only real false-positive case, observed at about 1.7% of Ruby targets on Rails, and valid code rarely hits it because a bare sibling-class constant is a Ruby NameError.

# Pascal const-param parse residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value refs accept a small residual false-positive tail where tree-sitter-pascal can context-dependently misparse a complex Delphi `const` parameter as `declConst`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says this parse-fidelity FP remains after restricting Pascal targets to `constant` only and is documented as an accepted caveat.

# Constant read node check

Lifecycle status: accepted

A new value-reference language must confirm the grammar node type used for constant reads before sweeping, because a reader-scan mismatch produces zero edges even when targets register correctly. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A names this as the PHP lesson: PHP constant references are `name` nodes, not `identifier` or `constant`, so edges did not form until `name` was added to `flushValueRefs`.

Top 5 recorded entries:

# Gin middleware chain tracing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph connects Go Gin middleware chains end-to-end in trace and explore so following a request reaches middleware and route handlers registered through `.Use()` and `.GET()` rather than dead-ending at framework dispatch. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 New Features.

# Gin middleware-chain synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph adds `ginMiddlewareChainEdges` to connect Gin's slice-index middleware dispatcher to every named HandlerFunc registered through `.Use`, `.GET`, and related route registration APIs. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says Gin's `(*Context).Next` dispatches through `c.handlers[c.index](c)`, tree-sitter cannot resolve that slice-index call, and the synthesizer finds the dispatcher and links it to registered named handlers, gated on the dispatcher existing, closures skipped, and capped.

# Gin agent rabbit-hole collapse

Lifecycle status: accepted

Gin middleware-chain synthesis turned prior agent rabbit-holing on `Context.Next` into clean CodeGraph runs, with no Read/Grep/Bash or Workflow calls in the WITH arm. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 reports Gin `callees(Next)` now surfaces Logger, Recovery, ErrorLogger, and handlers with stable node count, and Agent A/B flipped from a codegraph-negative rabbit-hole to clean runs with 38% fewer tool calls.

# Non-interface sibling detection

Lifecycle status: proposed

Adaptive explore should eventually detect sibling families that are not represented by `implements` or `extends` edges. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says Go `HandlerFunc` slices and function-pointer registries are not caught, and Gin's middleware chain does not trip the gate because its handlers are funcs rather than interface implementations.

# Declared return types define chain fit

Lifecycle status: accepted

The lesson from #750 is that chained-call support fits languages with reliably declared return types, not the broader or narrower label of statically typed languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says the original statically-typed README enumeration was incomplete and the through-line is reliable declared return types.

# Handler-array closure tracing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should recover flow from anonymous route handlers or lambdas when a framework route declaration has no named handler target. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 lists anonymous or closure route handlers as frontiers for Go inline `func(c){}` handlers, Rust anonymous `.to` closure handlers, Vapor closure handlers `app.get("x"){ }`, and Kotlin Ktor `routing { get("/x"){...} }` lambda handlers.

Lifecycle status: accepted

Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3c says Alamofire validation required callback-synthesizer `closureCollectionEdges`, pairing element-invoking collection iteration with same-field closure append sites globally by field name.

# Watch sync stale-edge tolerance

Lifecycle status: accepted

Watch sync drops a single stale edge instead of aborting the whole daemon sync with a `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` error. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

# Watch sync pipeline

Lifecycle status: accepted

The watch sync pipeline is CodeGraph's file-watcher and incremental synchronization layer that keeps the index aligned with filesystem edits, git pulls, branch switches, and MCP reconnects. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 releases 0.9.5 and 0.9.6 describe watcher excludes, filesystem-based change detection, catch-up on connect, debounce tuning, and stale-lock handling.

# Manual sync after watcher distrust

Lifecycle status: accepted

When live watching cannot be trusted, users must rely on `codegraph sync` or git sync hooks until auto-sync is restored. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says CodeGraph disables auto-sync once with a clear message instead of retrying forever or serving a stale index as healthy.

# Stale files must be named

Lifecycle status: accepted

When watcher-observed edits are not yet indexed, CodeGraph responses must tell the agent exactly which files are stale instead of silently serving a stale graph as fresh. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 releases 0.9.5 and 0.9.6 say tool responses add a warning banner naming stale files and watcher sync keeps files stale while another process holds the index lock.

Lifecycle status: accepted

A new value-reference language must confirm the grammar node type used for constant reads before sweeping, because a reader-scan mismatch produces zero edges even when targets register correctly. Lifecycle status: accepted

A small repo read-heavy result can be a fixable trace endpoint bug rather than an adoption floor; compare what the agent read with the tool output immediately before it. Lifecycle status: accepted

When trace names are common, start from the specific method node rather than a class name or broad symbol because trace can choose the wrong matching node. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 warns that common names such as `render` and `execute_sql` match many nodes, trace may start from the wrong one, and users should trace from the specific method rather than a class name.

Lifecycle status: accepted

# Config key-only indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes Spring configuration files by key only and omits their values from `codegraph_explore` and `codegraph_node` output; Shopify Liquid schema blocks are likewise indexed by name only. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 1.0.0 Security.

# Spring external config frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs config-key linkage beyond in-repo application/bootstrap config files, including `@PropertySource` external property files and Spring Cloud Config remote properties. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 lists those as Spring config-key linkage coverage frontiers after `@Value` and `@ConfigurationProperties` resolution shipped.

# Sensitive config summarization

Lifecycle status: accepted

File-view must summarize `yaml` and `properties` files by key rather than dumping their contents. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says security was preserved by summarizing yaml/properties by key and never dumping them, referencing #383.

# Remove CodeGraph config file

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph removed `.codegraph/config.json`, the related config API surface, and `.codegraphignore`; existing config files are ignored. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 Breaking Changes says the config file and config API were removed and `.codegraphignore` is no longer supported.

# C fn-pointer struct-field key

Lifecycle status: accepted

C fn-pointer dispatch synthesis must key registrations and indirect calls by the pair (struct type, function-pointer field) and only bridge when the receiver resolves to that struct type. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 says the shipped fn-pointer dispatch is keyed by (struct type, fn-pointer field), with receiver resolution from parameter/local type or unique-field fallback.
